historical_record.description: The Civil Works Administration's first San Francisco project, in December 1933, was to paint and remodel the interior of the ten-year-old State Building here: 36 men and $31,665. The Public Works Administration had set up its western district office in the same building that August, and the Works Progress Administration later took the remodelling up again, with interior painting, exterior ironwork, repairs to the north and east walls and new shelving. Some of that work is still visible inside.

Yerba Buena Cemetery, the city's first official public cemetery, covered a triangle bounded by the present Market, McAllister and Larkin Streets, including this block; the graves were moved to Lone Mountain by the mid-1860s and the ground became a public park.

The five-storey brick Supreme Court Building, built between 1888 and 1899, was the most prominent structure on the block before the earthquake, when small one- and two-storey frame buildings covered about ninety per cent of it.

Bliss & Faville won the design of the California State Building in a competition sponsored by the State Architect, held between August 1916 and February 1917 and open only to architects in California.

The six-storey California State Building was completed on the southern half of the block, a steel-frame building clad in Sierra White granite and terra cotta, to the design of Bliss & Faville. It is a contributory building in the Civic Center National Register district and was rated “5” in the 1976 city inventory.
Wing additions to the California State Building were completed, on the southern half of the block.

The Supreme Court room on the fourth floor of the California State Building — its most elaborate space, with a decorative skylight dome, coffered ceiling and ebony furnishings — was extensively remodelled, and a large mural by Arthur Mathews above the judges' bench was removed.
The seven-storey Annex was completed, a concrete-frame building clad in mosaic ceramic tile and ceramic veneer panels; work on it had begun in 1956.
The small commercial brick buildings on the north half of the block — stores, hotels, small businesses and automobile concerns rebuilt after 1906 — were demolished for the State Building Annex.

unknowns: The Planning Department's own reports disagree about the California State Building: the 1994 environmental impact report for the State's Civic Center complex gives 1922 in its summary and 1923 in its cultural resources chapter, while the 1991 Main Library and 1994 Courts Building reports both give 1926.
